Wislica Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Wiślica, Poland

Not demolished. Wiślica's Jewish community, first recorded in 1514, made up 63 percent of the town's population by 1921, most killed by the Germans at Treblinka in 1942. This cemetery, likely established in the second half of the 17th century, became a Holocaust execution and burial site during the war, including the shooting of a woman named Federman by gendarmes from Nowy Korczyn in fall 1942; that same year, the Germans forced Polish workers to pave a road to the railway station with some of its tombstones. In 2016, the Nissenbaum Family Foundation fenced the eastern portion of the site, co-financed by the Shpilski, Topel, and Land families of Wiślica.
